vocab.definition: Use evidence to judge how it went.
What a person thinks or feels.
A response that can help us improve.
Make a change that aims to help.

cases.text: An order slip records two drinks for table one.
cases.fact: The slip records the order, not its delivery.
cases.next_step: Check the handover record before claiming delivery.
cases.staff_note: Do not infer a correct delivery from an order alone.

cases.text: One guest wrote: The welcome felt calm.
cases.next_step: Keep the comment and say whose type of view it is.
cases.staff_note: Redact personal identifiers before shared use.

cases.text: A photo shows a clear service table.
cases.fact: The surface is visible at one moment.
cases.next_step: Use it for presentation, then seek other records for hygiene.
cases.staff_note: A photo alone does not establish all hygiene controls.

cases.text: No record shows who checked the last order.
cases.next_step: Mark the gap and ask staff for an existing record.
cases.staff_note: Never fill the gap by guessing a name or action.

cases.text: A staff note records a learner reading back an order.
cases.fact: The note records an observed action.
cases.next_step: Link it to communication and note any help.
cases.staff_note: Keep the actual observation and support detail.

cases.text: Someone says: Every customer was happy. There is no survey.
cases.fact: There is no record for the claim about everyone.
cases.next_step: Use only the feedback that exists.

The Theory · Reviewing our café service
Monday 30 November–Friday 4 December 2026 · lesson 1 of 2 · 40 minutes

The source assessment is retained. This lesson contributes evidence; it does not by itself complete an award. Public award labels are masked only.
Purpose and success checks
The weekly scheme line above is shared across two lessons. This lesson focuses on reviewing our café service.
What can our records tell us about the service?
I can find a fact in a real record. I can separate a view from a fact. I can suggest a change and give a reason.
VOC-W5-L1-E1: Individual evaluation linked to real service or rehearsal records, with a supported finding, a strength, a limit and a reasoned change. Fictional practice is labelled separately.
Before pupils arrive

Retrieve the actual Week 4 order sheets, role records, feedback and permitted work-only images. Mark whether the event was a real service or a rehearsal. If no service evidence exists, use the fictional cards for analysis and record the actual evidence gap. Do not present the fictional case as the learner’s service.
Offer processing time, a quiet start and the usual communication support. Capture each learner’s own work. Read the Staff Answers before teaching.
Calendar and continuity

Monday 30 November–Friday 4 December 2026. Two 40-minute lessons this week. No teaching day or clock slot is inferred. Any visitor, placement or external audience is unconfirmed; the in-class route is ready to use.
Staff enter the actual teaching date above. Continue the accepted prior-week evidence and support routines.

Access and practice
Supported: sort fact, view and gap with help. Independent: link a finding to its record. Aspire: explain a limit and a useful check.

Sort the six cards as fact, view or gap. Read records aloud where needed. Then each learner reviews their actual Week 4 service or rehearsal. If none exists, keep the fictional analysis as classroom work and add a clear missing-service note. Retain the original record beside the evaluation.

Begin evidence during practice and finish during capture. Accept speech, pointing, drawing, writing or usual AAC. Scribe exact words without supplying the assessed reason. No forced pair work or public performance.
Safe teaching evidence and learner voice
Boundaries

Use work-only records and redact customer names or contact details. Do not invent feedback, service completion or observed hygiene. This lesson handles records only; no food preparation or customer contact is required.
Unconfirmed slot and in class alternative

Unconfirmed. No booking, invitation, placement or event date is asserted. Use the fictional service cards and available classroom records. Label the work as an in-class review; keep missing actual-service evidence visible.
Assessment and feedback

Look for a specific record reference and an accurate claim about what it shows. A customer comment is a view from that customer, not a view from everyone. A proposed change needs a reason and a way to check it. Missing or rehearsal-only evidence remains explicit.

Retain actual work, response mode and support. Use VF · WS · I · NS+ (Yellow Box) · // (self-edit) · ? (read back) · R (responded) · E (evidence banked). R requires Voice, Audience, an NS+ prompt and the learner’s response in their own colour. Record E only after evidence is banked. Blank forms and adult models are not completed learner evidence.
Lundy moments
Space: calm, accessible participation. Voice: a choice, reason or help request. Audience: the adult listens or reads and replies. Influence: record the support or next-step change made in response.
Offer to the Communication portfolio
Explain a choice, listen to feedback and write or dictate a reflection. The receiving teacher maps authentic responses to their own Communication portfolio; no criteria are assigned here.

Staff answers and response guide
Reviewing our café service
These are possible responses and task guides, not learner observations. Accept a defensible answer based on the facts or actual work. Record each learner’s reasoning and support.

Model and hinge

Fictional example: Jo checks an order slip. The slip lists two drinks for table one. A note says one drink went to table two. Jo says: the handover needs a check. Next time, read back the table and order. A later record could show if this helps.
B. A photograph shows the visible scene at that moment. It does not prove every order or every guest response. Reteach by comparing a photo with a separate order slip, then use a fresh example.
Individual evidence key

Look for a specific record reference and an accurate claim about what it shows. A customer comment is a view from that customer, not a view from everyone. A proposed change needs a reason and a way to check it. Missing or rehearsal-only evidence remains explicit.
Feedback boundaries and next teaching
Card A: Do not infer a correct delivery from an order alone.
Card B: Redact personal identifiers before shared use.
Card C: A photo alone does not establish all hygiene controls.
Card D: Never fill the gap by guessing a name or action.
Card E: Keep the actual observation and support detail.
Card F: Accept a narrower supported statement.
Common misunderstandings
A photo cannot prove every hidden process. A happy comment from one person does not mean every guest was happy. Missing evidence is a gap, not a failure to hide.
Teaching boundary

Use work-only records and redact customer names or contact details. Do not invent feedback, service completion or observed hygiene. This lesson handles records only; no food preparation or customer contact is required.
Feedback

If a reason is missing, return to the fact or actual work. Re-model a different example, then keep the learner’s own revision. Use NS+ and the learner response in their own colour before R. E means evidence actually banked. Keep safeguarding records separate.
